ceiling_directive: Supply complete, checkable proofs of the native-optimizer coupling, centered higher-order aggregation, and fitted Hessian/weight stability bounds, with every norm contraction and uniform probability step derived from the stated primitive assumptions.
improvement_directive: Re-prove the native second-order transfer without the asserted coefficient-counting steps: explicitly establish equation (6) of the neighborhood coupling lemma, equations (3) and (8) of the centered-aggregate lemma, and equations (5) and (9) of the fitted-stability lemma. Then derive the Wald expansion and the rank-one corrected-remainder limit solely from those verified bounds.
critique: The proximal identity, three-block first differential, measurability argument, and score-diffuseness calculation are delivered, but the headline native-optimizer inference theorem is not proved. Its load-bearing bounds are introduced through informal coefficient counting: the neighborhood-coupling estimate (6), the ambient quadratic coefficient bounds and higher-order estimate (3)/(8), and fitted curvature and weight bounds (5)/(9) are asserted without derivations sufficient to establish uniformity or their stated powers of n, H, and the signal. The calibration does not repair this gap because its corrected native-optimizer remainder invokes the unproved transfer theorem, while its Hessian contraction formula (5) is itself stated after omitted algebra. The TL;DR and project justification therefore stale-overclaim feasible uniform Wald inference and a completed native second-order transfer as established results. On the results actually supported, this is a collection of useful setup lemmas rather than a field-level inference contribution, and the absence of a completed application or reproducible computation further limits the projected paper score.
